## Accounts to create
| Service | Plan / tier needed | Resources to create | Who owns the account |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mistral AI (console.mistral.ai) | A paid plan with API access to the models listed in 03_environment/01_prerequisites.md and the beta Agents, Libraries, Connectors and Workflows APIs | One API key for the platform (`MISTRAL_API_KEY`), plus one key per extra workspace. Nothing else needs creating by hand; agents, libraries and workflows are created by the app. | The operating organisation. Each workspace key may belong to a different Mistral workspace. |
| Microsoft Azure (optional) | Any subscription that can run a Standard_D4s_v5 VM | A resource group, a VM, an NSG with 22, 80 and 443 (`deploy/azure/create-vm.sh`), and optionally a DNS name for HTTPS | The deployer |
| NVIDIA Brev (optional) | An account with GPU or CPU instance quota | A CLI token and an org; instances are created by the app | The deployer |
| AWS, GCP, Azure or DigitalOcean (optional) | Credentials able to describe and start the target VMs | Accounts entered under Remote servers → provider accounts | The deployer |
| Neo4j | None (self-hosted community edition) | A container | n/a |

## Secrets
| Secret | Used by | Stored in | How to generate / obtain | Rotation impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MISTRAL_API_KEY` | Backend (Default workspace, background work), Tool Service | `backend/.env`, `tool-service/.env`, `deploy/.env` | Mistral console → API keys | Restart both services. The Default workspace uses the new key (`key_source=platform`). Resources created under the old key's Mistral workspace remain there. |
| Workspace Mistral keys | Backend, worker children | `auth_workspaces.key_ciphertext` (encrypted with the vault master keys) | Mistral console; entered at `/admin/workspaces` | `POST /admin/workspaces/{id}/rotate-key` takes `{api_key, allow_other_workspace}` and provisions the workspace again, unless the new key belongs to the same Mistral workspace. The worker picks the new key up at its next reconcile. |
| `VAULT_MASTER_KEYS` | Backend vault, workspace keys | Environment (`deploy/.env`), or the generated `backend/vault_key.secret` | `deploy.sh` generates one; or `POST /api/vault/generate-key`; or `python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"` | Put the new key first and keep the old ones, then `POST /api/vault/rotate-key` to re-encrypt. **Removing a key that still encrypts data makes those values and workspace keys unreadable.** |
| `REMOTE_SERVER_SECRET_KEY` | Remote-server and provider-account credentials | Environment, or the generated `backend/remote_servers_key.secret` | A Fernet key, as above | No rotation support. Changing it makes the stored credentials undecryptable ("Could not decrypt remote-server secrets (key changed?)"); re-enter them. |
| `ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD` | First start only | `backend/.env` | Choose one that meets the password policy | None after the first sign-in (the admin must change it) |
| `NEO4J_PASSWORD` (and `NEO4J_AUTH` for the container) | Backend, Neo4j | `backend/.env`, `deploy/.env` | `openssl rand -hex 16` (`deploy.sh` does this) | Neo4j keeps the password from its first start in its data volume. Changing it later needs a Neo4j password change or a fresh volume. |
| `VAULT_ADMIN_TOKEN` | Optional extra guard for vault operations | `backend/.env` | Any random string | Clients must send the new token |
| User credentials for tools (API keys and similar) | Generated tools and connectors at run time | Vault (`vault_secrets`), resolved per execution | Entered by users when a build asks, or on the Vault page | Versioned; rollback is possible (`/vault/secrets/{ref}/rollback`) |
| Connector credentials and OAuth | Mistral connectors | At Mistral (`/connectors/{id}/credentials`) | The third-party service | Managed at Mistral |
| Remote-server SSH keys, passwords and cloud credentials | Remote deployment | `remote_servers.secrets`, `remote_provider_accounts.secrets` (Fernet) | The provider | Re-enter them in the UI |
| Brev CLI login | Brev provisioning | The `brev-home` volume (`~/.brev`) | `docker compose exec backend brev login --token …` | Log in again |

Session cookies and invite or reset tokens are generated at run time and stored as hashes or ids in `auth_sessions` and `auth_tokens`. They are not configuration.

## Generated keys on first start
- **`backend/vault_key.secret`:** generated when `VAULT_MASTER_KEYS` is unset, with chmod 600 (best effort). It encrypts every vault value **and every workspace's Mistral key**. Losing it makes all of them unreadable: workspaces must be given their keys again, and vault secrets re-entered.
- **`backend/remote_servers_key.secret`:** generated when `REMOTE_SERVER_SECRET_KEY` is unset. Losing it loses the remote-server and provider-account credentials.
- **`deploy/.env`:** on the VM, `deploy.sh` writes generated values for `NEO4J_PASSWORD`, `REMOTE_SERVER_SECRET_KEY` and `VAULT_MASTER_KEYS` once. Back the file up.
- **Caddy certificates** are kept in the caddy-data volume (re-issued if lost, subject to Let's Encrypt rate limits).
- **The bootstrap admin row** is created from the environment. It is not a key, but without it (and without `python -m app.auth.cli create-admin`) nobody can administer the platform.
- **None of these files is committed:** `.gitignore` and `.dockerignore` exclude `*.secret`, `.env` and databases.
